utterances.text: Northwind Air, Anna speaking. Good morning!
Morning, Anna. This is Tom Keller from Brightline Facilities. We're refitting a meeting room on the third floor of an office we manage and the old extract fan just can't keep up.
Thanks for calling, Tom. Let's find the right replacement. How big is the room and how many people use it at once?
It's about ninety square metres, up to twenty-five people during workshops.
Got it. Do you know the duct size and roughly how long the duct run is?
Round duct, two hundred and fifty millimetres. The run is maybe eighteen metres with three bends and a grille at the end.

That helps a lot. For twenty-five people you'd want around twelve hundred cubic metres an hour, and with that run I'd estimate two hundred fifty pascals of pressure. Is noise a concern? It sounds like the fan sits above the ceiling of the room itself?
Yes, right above it. People complained the old one hums during presentations.
Then I'd go for an EC model, it's quieter and you can turn the speed down when the room is half empty. Do you need a speed controller on the wall, or will it run from the building management system?
BMS, ideally. We have a zero-to-ten volt output there.
Perfect, the EC fans take zero-to-ten volts directly. When does the refit need to be finished?
The contractor starts on the second of November.

Okay. My first choice is the NW-ID-250E, inline EC, two-fifty spigot, so no adapters. It covers twelve hundred cubic metres at two-fifty pascals with some reserve. It's in transit right now, the system shows arrival on the twenty-first of October, so we'd still be well ahead of the second.
And the price?
List price is three hundred fifty-five dollars. I'd also add a silencer on the room side, about ninety dollars, that's what really takes the hum away.
Hmm, the budget is tight. Is the silencer really needed?

Fair question. Without it you'd hear about fifty decibels in the room; with it, under forty. Since the complaint was exactly the hum, I'd keep it. If budget is the issue, the fan itself is the piece I would not downgrade.
Okay, makes sense. Can you send me a quote with both options, with and without the silencer?
Of course. I'll email the quote with both options and the fan curve by Thursday, the fifteenth, before noon. Is tom.keller at brightline dot com still the right address?
That's right.
Great. And I'll call you on Friday morning to go through it, if that suits you.
Friday works. Thanks, Anna.
Thank you, Tom. Have a good day.
